title: BreedingR: genetic parameters, breeding values and genomic prediction in R
description:
A self-contained R engine for quantitative genetic evaluation. It grew out of doctoral research. The numerics are written in the package itself, in C++ compiled by R CMD INSTALL, with no run-time dependency on any other package.

Variance components and breeding values. AI-REML with an analytic score, average information, EM warm-up and an EM rescue, walking in log-Cholesky coordinates so a covariance boundary is a limit rather than a wall; convergence certified by the Newton decrement of the off-boundary components, not by step size alone. Breeding values and their accuracy come from the same sparse factorisation through the selected inverse. A block Gibbs sampler fits the same designs, with a probit mode for binary traits.

Model families, written as formula terms. Animal model and repeatability; direct-maternal with the correlation between the two estimated; sire and maternal-grandsire models; reaction norms on a Legendre basis; multi-trait with a full residual matrix and missingness by pattern. The layout unit is the covariance group, which is what lets these share one engine.

Relationships. Pedigree A-inverse by Henderson's rules with Meuwissen-Luo inbreeding; metafounders with a full base relationship matrix, singular cases handled by the pseudo-inverse.

Genomics. Single-step with the exact G-inverse or APY; markers as equations by conjugate gradients (ssSNPBLUP), which never forms G; marker effects backsolved from the single-step fit; PLINK and BLUPF90 input.

Around the fit. Genotype and phenotype quality control that reports what it removed, heritability curves, genetic correlations, selection indices, rank drift, likelihood profiles, standard errors of arbitrary functions of the components, thermal indices for heat-stress work, MCMC diagnostics and a gene-dropping simulator.
